items.text: REFERRED TO CIVIL SERVICE AND PENSIONS

items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the civil service law and the civil practice law and rules, in
relation to the grounds for which the public employment relations board may
seek injunctive relief
items.lawCode: Amd §209-a, Civ Serv L; amd §§6301 & 6313, CPLR
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8182

SPONSOR: SAVINO
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the civil service law and the civil practice law and
rules, in relation to the grounds for which the public employment
relations board may seek injunctive relief

 
PURPOSE:

To provide a clearer definition of the standard to apply when injunctive
relief is sought by the New York State Public Relations Board in New
York State Supreme Court.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

§ 1 - adds a definition to subdivision 4 to section 209-a of the civil
service law - Injunctive Relief, for purposes of determining, irrepara-
ble injury, loss or damage, shall mean, but not be limited to loss of
employment, actions that adversely affect the health and welfare, or
permanent loss of an employee right or privilege established pursuant to
a collective bargaining agreement.

§ 2 - adds a definition to section 6301 of the civil practice law and
rules that directs the Supreme Court to apply the definitions of section
209-a-4 when determining appropriate grounds from which to issue a
preliminary injunction.

 
EXISTING LAW:

Section 1 of this act addresses a disparity in current law that prevents
the New York State Public Employment Relations Board from applying its
regulatory authority to seek injunctive relief after it determines that
a party has committed a labor violation pursuant civil service law.
Hence, a definition has been added to address under what auspices is
considered irreparable injury, or loss or damage to include specific
actions that has been determined by PERB to be irreparable injury to
warrant its authority to seek injunctive relief.

Section 2 of this act provides for directive of Supreme Court in deter-
mining the merits of issuing a preliminary injunction to apply the same
definition of irreparable injury as defined under section 209-a-4 of the
civil service law.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Historically, our State has deferred to the Public Employment Relations
Board as a matter of public policy to act as the primary agency to
determine labor disputes between public employees and their government
employers. For over 50 years, PERB has maintained its exemplary status
as the main cause in maintaining labor peace throughout our State and as
such, great deference is given to PERB by all branches of government
when it renders decisions on disputed labor issues. In fact, the legis-
lature has permitted PERB to seek injunctive relief in certain instances
when it determines the actions to be irreparable harm. Unfortunately,
PERB'S decisions sometimes conflicts with the CPLR in defining what is
"irreparable harm". This clearer definition will act to provide a

consistent course from which both PERB and our courts can navigate in
providing consistency under the law.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

None.
